title: enterprise-commit-and-billing-controls-framework-2026
author: Marisol Chen
body:
Purpose
-------
This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s Enterprise Commit and Billing Controls Framework: end-to-end rules for how we accept customer financial commitments, how we manage contract amendments, how procurement and vendor billing interact with revenue recognition, and the operational controls that prevent revenue leakage or accounting exceptions. It targets Finance, Legal, Sales Ops, Revenue Ops, and Engineering teams that integrate with billing and contract workflows.

Scope and audience
------------------
Applies to: customer contracts (hosted API, Dedicated reservations, Private deployments), vendor procurement, and internal purchase commitments exceeding $25k ARR or $50k CAPEX equivalent. Not a substitute for Legal review: all contract template changes must be routed to Legal per the Contract Change Procedure.

Key principles
--------------
- Single source of truth: customer commercial terms live in the CLM (Contract Lifecycle Management) system and the billing system (Stripe/Zuora mirror).
- Separation of duties: Sales negotiates commercial terms; Legal approves non-standard terms; Finance approves revenue treatment and AMs (amendments) > $100k ARR; Billing implements configuration and invoices.
- Revenue SRO (Single Responsible Owner): finance-legal team owns revenue recognition decisions and deferred revenue schedules.
- Minimal manual adjustments: changes to invoicing/deferral should be automated; manual journals must have RCA and approval.

Controls matrix (high-level)
---------------------------
| Control area | Owner | Threshold | Evidence required | Frequency |
|--------------|-------|-----------|-------------------|-----------|
| Contract approval (standard templates) | Legal | any | Signed contract in CLM | Per contract |
| Contract approval (non-standard terms) | Legal + Finance | Any non-template clause or > $100k ARR | Redlined contract + approval record | Per contract |
| Revenue recognition treatment signoff | Finance | > $50k ARR | Revenue memo + schedule | Per deal |
| Billing configuration change | Billing ops | Any | Config change ticket ID + test invoice | Per change |
| Procurement vendor onboarding | Procurement | > $25k/year | Vendor W-9, SSF, security attestation | Per vendor |
| Invoice dispute > $10k | Revenue ops | > $10k | Dispute case + remediation plan | As needed |

(Represented above as a table — the source of truth is the Controls spreadsheet in Finance Drive.)

Budgeting, Forecasting, and Commit Treatment
-------------------------------------------
1) Budget windows and cutoffs
   - Quarterly operating budget windows: Q1-Q4 planning opens 8 weeks prior to quarter start.
   - Booking cutoff for revenue forecast inclusion: deals signed and in CLM by the final business day of the quarter are eligible for recognition in that quarter subject to delivery/acceptance terms.

2) Forecast categories and flags
   - Committed: Signed, countersigned, invoiceable (CLM + billing config completed).
   - Provisionally Committed: Signed but pending billing config or KYC/security checks. Flagged as PENDING_BILLING.
   - Pipeline: Term sheet or verbal commitment only — not recognizeable.

3) Treatment rules for dedicated capacity and prepayments
   - Upfront prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and amortized over the contracted service period. Example: $120k upfront for 12 months -> $10k recognized monthly.
   - Overprovision credits (e.g., reserved capacity discounts) are recorded as contra-revenue and applied pro rata unless the agreement specifies otherwise.

Contract Amendments and Change Management
-----------------------------------------
Procedure (step-by-step):
1. Sales submits Amendment Request in CLM and tags Legal + Finance.
2. Legal reviews redlines; if non-standard customer language is required, Legal documents the risk and assigns an approver.
3. Finance evaluates impact on revenue recognition (cash vs accrual, deferral windows) and approves proposed accounting treatment on the amendment.
4. Contract is countersigned and CLM status set to AMENDED.
5. Billing ops executes billing configuration changes (new payment terms, discounts, invoice dates) in billing system and marks change ticket with CLM amendment ID.
6. Revenue ops runs a pre-production invoice to a shadow customer account for any new billing cadence or price changes; results attached to the amendment record.
7. If accounting treatment changes materially (see Materiality thresholds), a revenue memo is archived and a journal entry created at period close.

Materiality thresholds
- Financial impact > $50k in a quarter OR changes ARR recognition > 2% of last 12 months revenue for the customer -> requires Finance Director signoff and memo.
- Any change that introduces multi-element arrangements requires Revenue Ops + Finance to map deliverables and recognition patterns.

Procurement interaction and vendor billing policies
--------------------------------------------------
- Procurement must route all vendor contracts > $25k through the supplier onboarding flow, capturing security attestation and pricing schedules.
- Capitalizable hardware/infrastructure purchases: Procurement tags POs as CAPEX; Finance-Procurement monthly review determines capitalization.
- Invoice review: AP team matches 3-way (PO, receipt, invoice) where applicable. Exceptions must be documented and escalated to Procurement Manager.

Billing operations and invoice lifecycle
-------------------------------------
Invoice cadence and types
- Monthly usage invoices (hosted API usage): emailed by the 7th business day following month close; thresholded auto-invoice enabled for customers with payment method on file.
- Advance/renewal invoices: generated 30 days before subscription renewal for annual/commit contracts.
- One-time invoices: generated when deliverables (onboarding, professional services) are accepted.

Dispute and remediation process
1. Customer raises a billing dispute (Support or Sales ticket).
2. Revenue Ops triages within 48 hours and acknowledges receipt.
3. If validation confirms a billing error, Revenue Ops issues a credit memo and adjusts deferred revenue schedules if needed.
4. If the dispute requires contract interpretation, Legal engages and delivers an opinion within 10 business days.
5. Record of dispute and resolution is attached to the CLM and the customer account.

Revenue recognition policy highlights
----------------------------------
- Revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606 principles (or equivalent IFRS 15): identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price, recognize when (or as) performance obligations satisfied.
- Standalone selling prices: use observable list prices where available; otherwise use an internal SSP matrix maintained by Finance (SSP matrix file path referenced in related pages).
- Multi-element arrangements: allocate on a relative standalone selling price basis and recognize over the period when control of each deliverable transfers.
- Deferred revenue schedule: generated per contract in the close process and reconciled weekly.

Monitoring, KPIs and Reporting
----------------------------
Primary KPIs (monitored weekly/monthly):
- Forecast accuracy (Bookings vs Recognized Revenue) — target: <= 5% variance quarter-over-quarter.
- Time from contract signing to billing activation — target: <= 7 business days.
- Number of billing disputes > $5k per month — target: 0.
- Deferred revenue reconciliation exceptions — target: 0 exceptions unresolved > 2 business days.

Operational runbooks and escalation paths
---------------------------------------
- Billing activation runbook: step-by-step checklist (CLM ID, payment method verification, tax determination, invoice preview, test invoice). Owner: Billing Ops.
- Revenue memo template: includes background, impact analysis, deferred schedule, and GL impact lines. Owner: Finance Accounting.
- Escalation: any unresolvable billing issue after 3 business days escalates to Head of Revenue Ops; material accounting disputes escalate to CFO and General Counsel.

Templates and examples (appendix)
--------------------------------
1) Example deferred schedule (ascii table):
| Period | Amount recognized | Deferred balance |
|-------:|------------------:|-----------------:|
| 2026-03 | $10,000 | $110,000 |
| 2026-04 | $10,000 | $100,000 |
| ... | ... | ... |

2) Example amendment ticket checklist:
- CLM amendment ID
- Redline + summary of change
- Finance accounting impact statement
- Billing test invoice ID
- Legal approval stamp

Glossary of key terms
---------------------
- CLM: Contract Lifecycle Management system (source of truth for signed agreements).
- PENDING_BILLING: Flag used in CRM for deals awaiting billing configuration.
- Deferred revenue: cash received in advance of service delivery recorded as liability.
- SSP: Standalone Selling Price.

Next steps and open actions
--------------------------
- Finance to publish the SSP matrix and upload the Revenue Memo template to Finance Drive by 2026-03-01.
- Billing Ops to automate the PENDING_BILLING flag resolution workflow (owner: Billing SRE) by 2026-04-15.
- Procurement to update supplier onboarding to collect security attestation for all vendors storing customer data by 2026-03-31.

Document ownership and review cadence
-------------------------------------
Owner: Finance (Revenue Accounting) — Marisol Chen (Document owner for operational updates).
Review cadence: quarterly review (content + thresholds) and ad-hoc when new product billing models are introduced (e.g., per-token streaming pricing changes).
